title: By Whom Was David Taught
description: By Whom Was David Taught in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 17, “Jehovah-Nissi, The Lord my banner. Ex 17:15”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: By whom was Da-vid taught, To aim the dread-ful blow, When he Go-li-ath fought, And laid the Git-tite low? No sword nor spear the stri-pling took, But chose a peb-ble from the brook.

lines: No sword nor spear the stripling took,
But chose a pebble from the brook.
Who sent him to the fight;
Who gave him strength to fling,
Ye feeble saints your strength endures,
Because young David's God is yours.
The trumpets made his coming known,
And all the host was overthrown.
Oh! I have seen the day,
My trust is in the Lord;
My soul has quelled a thousand foes,
Fearless of all that could oppose.
Yet David's Lord, and Gideon's friend,
Will help his servant to the end.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
